thread:
jen_support: FYI customer ACME (private deployment in us-east-1) opened a P0 — intermittent 502s and TLS timeouts to their private API endpoint. They say it started after provider maintenance ~02:00 UTC. ticket #78912 :eyes:
leo_infra: Can you paste a curl/traceroute from their VPC or a host in the same subnet?
jen_support: From their dev host: ```
$ curl -v https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/health
*   Trying 10.244.5.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.244.5.12 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to private-api.acme.internal port 443: Connection timed out
```
dan_networks: traceroute from the same host: ```
traceroute to private-api.acme.internal (10.244.5.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.1.1  0.4 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms
 2  tgw-0a1b2c3d (172.31.0.1)  1.2 ms 1.1 ms 1.1 ms
 3  dx-peer-01.provider.net (203.0.113.1)  4.8 ms 4.7 ms 4.6 ms
 4  198.51.100.200  20.3 ms 20.1 ms 20.2 ms
 5  * * *
```
leo_infra: hop 5 is odd — looks like traffic leaves provider and then drops. Are you seeing BGP prefixes for the /24 containing 10.244.5.0/24 on the provider side?
jen_support: customer shared their on-prem edge BGP summary: ```
BGP router identifier 192.0.2.10, local AS 65001
Neighbor 203.0.113.2 remote AS 65002 up 01:23:45
  Received prefixes 1, Advertised prefixes 1
  Prefixes: 10.244.0.0/16 (aggregated)
```
priya_pm: they lost the /24 specifics — only seeing the /16 aggregate. Could that explain reachability holes?
dan_networks: yes — if we only see the aggregated /16 on the peering side the provider may be filtering the specific /24s. That would cause traffic to be forwarded to a different next-hop (or dropped) for subnets that rely on more specific routes.
leo_infra: Can the customer run `show ip bgp 10.244.5.0/24` on their router and also ask their DX provider for the NLRI they are receiving from ACME's ASN?
jen_support: customer result: ```
show ip bgp 10.244.5.0/24
No BGP entry for 10.244.5.0/24
show ip bgp 10.244.0.0/16
10.244.0.0/16  via 203.0.113.2, external, valid
```
leo_infra: provider-side route filters often deny prefixes shorter than or longer than certain masks. Looks like a route-filter or route-map was applied during the provider maintenance that stripped the /24s. I suspect a customer or provider ACL denies prefixes with mask /24 (or conversely allows only aggregates).
dan_networks: action plan: 1) Ask provider to confirm received NLRI from our ASN and whether they applied any route-filters during the maintenance. 2) In parallel, request provider to temporarily advertise the exact /24s (or remove the filter) as a mitigation. 3) If provider-side change not possible immediately, we can push a temporary static route+BGP advertisement for the missing /24s from the DX peer (needs coordination).
jen_support: raised a request with provider NOC, they replied: "we applied an inbound route-policy to collapse customer prefixes into aggregates for transit optimization during the maintenance, will revert on approval." They need our confirmation of which exact /24s must be preserved.
priya_pm: list of critical subnets for API: `10.244.5.0/24`, `10.244.7.0/24`, `10.244.12.0/24` — shared with provider.
leo_infra: while provider works the change, request temporary workaround: change route-reflector policy to advertise the three /24s explicitly (we can do that from our side) — needs ops approval.
ops-bot: deployment request #dx-temp-announce created by leo_infra — awaiting approval.
leo_infra: I'm going to prepare a safe policy that only announces the specific /24s rather than broad /16 to avoid route leakage. Will apply as emergency change with watch.
dan_networks: also ask them to check any ACL/firewall on provider-edge that might drop traffic destined to more-specific prefixes — but primary is the filter.
jen_support: provider reverted the route-policy for affected ASN at 1835123600 and confirmed NLRI now includes the /24s. They say it was an overzealous optimization rule.
leo_infra: confirm from our side `show ip bgp summary` now shows Received prefixes: 3 for that ASN and `show ip bgp 10.244.5.0/24` returns path.
jen_support: customer re-tested curl at 1835123680: ```
$ curl -v https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/health
* Connected to 10.244.5.12 (10.244.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* Server certificate: CN=private-api.acme.internal
* HTTP/1.1 200 OK
"ok"
```
priya_pm: nice. Follow-ups: 1) provider to update runbook to avoid blanket aggregate policy during maintenance, 2) we should document this specific customer symptom (TLS/timeouts + /16 aggregate present) as a KB, 3) update DX onboarding checklist to validate route-filter behavior.
leo_infra: will create KB and a short postmortem note. Also recommend provider implement a BGP community to signal "preserve-more-specifics" so this doesn't happen again.
jen_support: marking incident mitigated — waiting for provider postmortem and KB link. Will keep thread open until those items done. :thumbsup:
